html:
A famine that struck almost all of Iran from 1870 to 1872, under the Qajar shah Naser al-Din. It is the best documented famine in Iranian history.

Drought and failed harvests set it off. Other causes made it worse. During the American Civil War cotton prices had soared, and many farmers had moved from grain to cotton and opium, which could be sold abroad. Landlords and officials hoarded grain and sold it at high prices, and roads were too poor to bring food from regions that had it. Cholera and typhus followed hunger.

How many died is unknown. Estimates vary widely, from a few hundred thousand to well over a million, out of a population of perhaps six to ten million. A few towns, such as Shahrud, Kerman and Birjand, escaped.

The famine weakened the shah's government and fed criticism of the Qajar state. A worse famine came during World War I, the famine of 1917 to 1919.
sum: A famine that struck almost all of Iran from 1870 to 1872, under the Qajar shah Naser al-Din. It is the best documented famine in Iranian history.
